# Fastidious Gram-negatives and Gram-negative cocci

> *Why do some bacteria need special food, and why do fragile bacteria spread only by close contact?*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
This chapter will follow the same template as the *Gram-positive cocci* chapter. The outline below
shows what it will cover.
:::

**The group in one sentence:** Gram-negative bacteria that depend on their host for nutrients, or die quickly outside it.

**How members differ (the sorting key):** Growth needs (enriched media); fragility outside the body; capsule.

**Main organisms (full profile cards):** *Neisseria meningitidis* (capsule in the blood), *Neisseria gonorrhoeae* (fragility, antigenic variation), *Haemophilus influenzae* (factors from blood).

**Supporting organisms (one table row each):** *Bordetella pertussis*, *Legionella*, *Moraxella*, the HACEK group.

**Later in the course:** Meningitis, gonorrhoea, whooping cough and Legionnaires disease in the organ blocks.
